facts.fact: Convention of 18 Nov 1903; a zone ten miles wide, five miles on each side of the centre line
facts.known_by_basis: Convention text, IA panamacanalmessa00unit, Arts. II-III

facts.fact: Art. III: the rights "which the United States would possess and exercise if it were the sovereign"
Panama and Colon excluded from the grant
Obaldía to Hay, 11 Aug 1904
Roosevelt received by Amador, 15 Nov 1906
Three days on the Isthmus; the second in the Culebra Cut; he questioned laborers
More than 2 1/3 million cubic yards a month, winter 1908; 103 steam shovels
Lock canal, summit level 85 feet
Goethals's 1909 paper
30 Apr 1908: 33,193 at work, 5,831 gold and 27,362 silver
The Canal Record went free to gold roll employees
Gorgas, chief sanitary officer
October 1906 deaths as the message gives them
Women in government houses, May 1908: 1,290, 237 and 1,104
Boswell on the Isthmus, Sep-Oct 1907, founding women's clubs
Gamboa dike blown, 10 Oct 1913
The crane boat Alex. LaValley (the Record's form) passed through the locks at Pedro Miguel and Miraflores, 7 Jan 1914, the first steam vessel through from ocean to ocean
facts.known_by_basis: Canal Record VII no. 20, 7 January 1914, 'First Steam Vessel Through the Canal' (OCR; masthead confirmed, text verification 8 Nov 2026); NARA 100995584 caption

facts.fact: The Ancon's official trip, 15 Aug 1914, about 9 hours, Porras aboard
Garrison's cable of 15 Aug 1914
Stock floated Dec 1880; liquidator appointed 4 Feb 1889; work suspended 15 May 1889; New Panama Canal Co. organised Oct 1894
On 9 Feb 1889 Lesseps announced he could not form a new company
By 24 May 1889 the Jamaican commissioner had sent away about 4,000 people, with 3,000 tickets more
facts.known_by_basis: Seattle Post-Intelligencer, 25 May 1889, p. 1, 'PANAMA, May 24.' (page image: 4,000 and 3,000); The Freeman, 1 June 1889, p. 6, 'A Smash at Panama' (page image; its digits are broken type, read against the P-I; text verification, 8 Nov 2026)

facts.fact: Walker Commission valued the French property at $40,000,000

The Isthmian Canal Commission's supplementary report of 18 January 1902, after the New Panama Canal Company offered its rights, property and unfinished work for $40,000,000, found "the most practicable and feasible route" to be the Panama route, with the lock plan of its former report
facts.known_by_basis: Report of the Isthmian Canal Commission upon the proposition of the New Panama Canal Company, dated Washington, D. C., 18 January 1902, transmitted to Congress 20 January 1902 (57th Congress, 1st session, Senate Document 123): the offer p. 2, the recital of the report of 16 November 1901 pp. 6-7, the opinion and signatures p. 10 (govinfo SERIALSET-04230_00_00-026-0123-0000, page images). Goethals 1909, p. 3 compresses the two reports into one and is not the basis (round 2, 8 Nov 2026)

facts.fact: Navy ordered on 2 Nov 1903 to keep the transit open and prevent hostile landings; about 400 Colombian troops at Colon, 3 Nov
Uprising, evening of 3 Nov 1903, "no bloodshed"; independence proclaimed; Junta of Arango, Boyd and Arias
The US entered into relations with the de facto government, 6 Nov 1903
Colombia protested on 7 Nov (Herrán) and 23 Dec 1903 (Reyes)
1904 Constitution, Art. 136, allows US intervention
Taft in Panama, Nov-Dec 1904; banquet on 1 Dec
Executive Order of 5 Dec 1912: all Zone land necessary; possession directed
Towns between Gorgona and Gatun cleared; Gorgona district abolished by EO of 2 Sep 1912
facts.known_by_basis: ICC Annual Report 1913, Dept. of Law

facts.fact: Moving Gorgona: 200 American families, 600 bachelors, several hundred West Indians, Mar-Jun 1913
30 Jun 1913: 23,184 in commission quarters (9,173 gold, 4,295 European, 9,716 West Indian)
Largest force 44,733 on 26 Mar 1913 (gold 5,993, silver 38,740)
45,107 laborers brought to the Isthmus since the start, 11,873 from Cuba and Europe, "the balance from Colombia and the West Indies"
Gatun Lake at elevation 31 on 1 Jul 1912, 56.28 ft on 29 Nov 1912; sluices closed 27 Jun 1913
Gatun Locks first operated 26 Sep 1913 (the tug Gatun, west flight)
facts.known_by_basis: Canal Record VII no. 6, 1 October 1913 (page image; masthead confirmed, text verification 8 Nov 2026)

facts.fact: Gamboa dike fired at 2.02 p.m., 10 Oct 1913, by Wilson at Washington by telegraph; a cayuco passed first

The Central Division removed 109,163,547 cu yd from the territory of the Central Division, 4 May 1904 to August 1913, including all accessory work (105,743,176 of them from the canal prism), with about 38,729,000 lb of explosives
facts.known_by_basis: Canal Record VII no. 6, 1 October 1913, p. 49 (the rows and the earth-plus-rock total both sum to 109,163,547; text verification, 8 Nov 2026)

facts.fact: Gaillard left ill 9 Aug 1913; died at Baltimore 5 Dec 1913
The Ancon's timetable, 15 Aug 1914: Cristobal 7.10 a.m.; Gatun 8.00; Gamboa 11.15; Cucaracha 12.20; Pedro Miguel 12.56; Miraflores 1.56-3.20; channel's end 4.30 p.m.; about 200 guests
17,949 Barbadians recruited to 7 Jul 1909, of 27,500 West Indians recruited
A Barbados medical examiner found taking fees from laborers
Barbados prohibited further recruiting
facts.known_by_basis: Canal Record IV, 19 Jul 1911; V, 20 Sep 1911

facts.fact: 528 laborers recruited in Barbados, Jan-Feb 1913
Ten cents an hour for all West Indian laborers
Europeans paid 16, then 20, cents gold an hour
Canal medals cast from copper of old French excavators and locomotives, for two years' service
Medal and longevity pay for US citizens only
facts.known_by_basis: Canal Record II, 16 Dec 1908 and 10 Feb 1909

facts.fact: 14,822 money orders ($429,990.47) issued in Sep 1908

facts.known_by_basis: ICC 1913, App. P (Gorgas); figures from the page image

facts.fact: The Governor's monthly report for May 1914 (Culebra, 18 June 1914; printed in the Canal Record VII no. 45, 1 July 1914, p. 450) gives as the reason for the whites' much higher admission and noneffective rates that whites receive pay for 24 days a year while sick from disease and blacks do not; the Record states no rule
facts.known_by_basis: Canal Record VII no. 45, 1 July 1914, p. 450, 'Canal Work in May', Department of Health (page image; text verification, 8 Nov 2026)

facts.fact: Clubhouse for colored men at Culebra opened 3 Nov 1911, used until spring 1913
Lake-area villages (Bohio, Frijoles, San Pablo, Tabernilla) sold or demolished, "a colored schoolhouse" among them
San Pablo-Tabernilla vacated
Joint Land Commission (Federico Boyd, Roland P. Falkner, Samuel Lewis, L. S. Rowe) made awards for houses in Gorgona and Cruces (e.g. Juan Sotillo, Gabriel Jolly)
Former owners in native Gorgona denied free transport for their houses' material
United Fruit recruited 327 laborers in two weeks, over 90% British West Indians
Five West Indian masons laid 96,000 bricks in a day at Balboa, at 13 cents an hour
Trained female nurses only at the Colon and Ancon hospitals; Ancon had 500 beds, 61 nurses
facts.known_by_basis: Freeland, 'Nursing in the Canal Zone', AJN 7, June 1907: trained female nurses only at Colon and Ancon, p. 697; 500 beds and 61 nurses, p. 699 as read on the image (the IA OCR's leaf numbering places the sentence a page earlier; the image governs) (text verification, 8 Nov 2026)

facts.fact: A committee of Havana's Gallego Society inspected the Spanish laborers
Camera flights over the canal by hydro-biplane, 25 and 27 Apr 1913, with R. A. Duhem of the Duhem and Harter Motion Picture Company; Balboa 10.00 to Cristobal 10.57
Taft was to leave Washington on 19 Dec 1912 for Key West; he arrived at Cristobal on the Arkansas on 24 Dec and sailed on 26 Dec on the Delaware under convoy of the Arkansas
facts.known_by_basis: Canal Record VI no. 18, 25 December 1912, and no. 19, 1 January 1913 (text verification, 8 Nov 2026)

facts.fact: The SS Ancon came into Cristobal with 1,500 laborers from Barbados, 2 Sep 1909
facts.known_by_basis: NARA 100996834 (185-G-1127) caption; Canal Record III, September 1909: "The steamship Ancon, which arrived on September 2, brought 1,500 Barbadian laborers" (OCR; text verification, 8 Nov 2026)

facts.fact: Lesseps visited the Isthmus in February 1886 and wrote of it on his return ("the voyage which I have just made")
facts.known_by_basis: Lesseps, Recollections of Forty Years, tr. Pitman, London 1887, vol. I, pp. 141-151; the date of the visit (arrival 17 February 1886) from Bunau-Varilla 1913, pp. 57-59. The translator's note 'This chapter was written in 1885' (p. 150) dates the Suez sentence, not the visit (text verification, 8 Nov 2026)

facts.fact: The Canal Record, the Commission's weekly, first issue dated 4 Sep 1907
facts.known_by_basis: The Canal Record vol. I no. 1, 4 Sep 1907, masthead (IA canalrecord1152isth; the brief's section 8 and the 'no distinction' card)

facts.fact: Bunau-Varilla was an engineer of the French company at Colon in 1885 ("my house at Colon")
facts.known_by_basis: Bunau-Varilla, Panama: the Creation, Destruction, and Resurrection, 1913, pp. 43-44 (added from the brief's R13 source)

facts.fact: The Isthmian Canal Commission's report of 16 November 1901 found "the most practicable and feasible route" to be the Nicaragua route, the New Panama Canal Company's price of $109,141,500 for its property being "so unreasonable that its acceptance can not be recommended"; a canal with locks on either route
facts.known_by_basis: Report of the Isthmian Canal Commission, 1899-1901 (57th Congress, 1st session, Senate Document 54), p. 263, the conclusion and signatures dated 16 November 1901 (IA reportofisthmian07unit, OCR; the signatures' page break to confirm on the image)
